messages:
leah_sales: FinServCorp SQ says they need: immutable audit logs, static egress IPs for allowlist, TLS inspection in their DMZ, and preservation of client source IP for fraud detection. POC target next Thu. Can we map recommended network options + what breaks TLS inspection? Also need quick note for procurement on POC pricing impact.

ben_sre: TL;DR options we should present (ranked by ops friction -> preserving src IP):
- Option A: VPC Peering / Transit Gateway (preserves native src IP). Pros: full src IP, simpler for firewall rules. Cons: needs cross-account routing, peering approvals, possible egress data transfer costs.
- Option B: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) + our egress NAT (default) -> source IPs come from our EIP pool. Pros: simple customer changes, no route approvals. Cons: loses layer3 client IP.
- Option C: PrivateLink + customer proxy that consumes X-Forwarded-For / Proxy Protocol v2 inserted by our edge. Pros: preserves application-level identity without routing changes. Cons: requires app/proxy change on customer side to trust and log XFF/ProxyProtocol.

mira_neteng: Important TLS inspection note: if FinServCorp insists on decrypt-and-inspect in their DMZ, they must terminate TLS -> they will see our client certs only if mutual TLS is used or if we present TLS to their proxy. Two subpatterns:
- TLS passthrough (SNI-only inspection): their box sees SNI and IP, can't inspect HTTP body or validate our mTLS. This works with PrivateLink but doesn't allow body inspection.
- TLS terminate-and-forward: their proxy terminates TLS and re-establishes TLS to us. This breaks end-to-end client certificate verification unless we adopt mutual TLS with client certs they manage.

mira_neteng: We can support an HMAC-signed X-Client-IP header inserted at our edge (for POC only) so they can trust an injected client identity without terminating TLS. Requires: (a) their proxy must accept the header, (b) we share HMAC key rotation plan.

ben_sre: Firewall ports checklist for POC (customer inbound rules to their proxy / firewall):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 -> our privatelink DNS name or EIP pool (if static IPs requested).
- Allow UDP/TCP 53 -> for DNS (if they resolve our hostname locally).
- Allow NTP UDP 123 -> time sync for cert validation (optional but recommended).
- Ephemeral return ports 1024-65535 (stateful) or explicit ephemeral range if they use stateless ACLs.
- If they use Proxy Protocol v2: allow the TCP flow and configure their proxy to parse v2 headers.

leah_sales: Procurement question: If we provide 3 static EIPs for the week-long POC, what are the cost signals? Any blocking enterprise approvals?

mira_neteng: POC pricing caveat: publishing 3 EIPs typically means we run those through NAT Gateway or similar. On AWS that means NAT Gateway hourly + per-GB egress charges. For PrivateLink theres also endpoint-hour + data processing fee. For Dedicated Private installs we may incur reserved capacity pricing. For sales: we can offer up to 50GB complimentary POC egress and a 72-hour free endpoint-hours waiver, after which normal billing applies. Please get legal signoff if they want indemnities for the complimentary credit.

ben_sre: Security questionnaire answers to prep (short bullets we can paste into SQ):
- Q: Will customer be able to see original client IP? A: Yes if using VPC peering / TGW. If using PrivateLink, our service will source requests from a small egress IP set; we can provide an application-level header (X-Client-IP) signed for authenticity or use Proxy Protocol where supported.
- Q: Can TLS be inspected by customer? A: They can inspect SNI only if TLS passthrough is used; to inspect body they must terminate TLS in their DMZ and re-establish a TLS session to us. Mutual TLS is supported and recommended for strong auth patterns.
- Q: Will logs/audit data be immutable? A: We provide append-only write-once logs with retention controls in our Console; for Private deployments these can be integrated into the customer's SIEM via secure forwarders.

leah_sales: Nice. Two quick asks: (1) a 1-page diagram for each pattern we can drop in the SQ; (2) a short copy-paste firewall allowlist we can give their infra team. Can someone own?

mira_neteng: I'll own diagrams and include a small ASCII diagram + bullet callouts. Will post by EOD.

ben_sre: I'll draft the SQ copy-paste firewall text and the procurement-facing pricing blurb.

deploy_bot: Reminder: add POC calendar slot Thu 09:30-11:30 and tag infra oncall.

leah_sales: Thx team. I'll ask FinServCorp whether they can accept signed X-Client-IP header + mTLS for the POC as that avoids peering approvals. If they decline we'll scope TGW/peering and loop in NetOps for routing approvals. :white_check_mark:
